newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UK JUDGE RE-EXAMINES HILLSBOROUGH DEATHS EVIDENCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UK JUDGE RE-EXAMINES HILLSBOROUGH DEATHS EVIDENCE.

text.p: The British government asked a senior judge on Monday to investigate whether an inquiry should be reopened into the 1989 Hillsborough tragedy, when 96 football fans were crushed to death at a soccer match.

Home Secretary Jack Straw, Britain's interior minister, told parliament that he had asked Lord Justice Stuart Smith to examine if there was new video and medical evidence to warrant a further public inquiry into the disaster.
"We owe it to everyone touched by the tragedy, but above all to the families of those who died, to get to the bottom of this matter once and for all," Straw said.

A television documentary last December claimed to have found new evidence about the disaster, which happened at a cup semi-final match between Nottingham Forest and Liverpool at the Hillsborough stadium in Sheffield, northern England.
The programme revived calls for a re-examination of police conduct at Hillsborough and greater compensation for relatives of the dead, who were all Liverpool fans.

But Straw's predecessor at the Home Office, Michael Howard, had said he would not reopen the inquiry unless he was convinced it would be in the public interest. Howard's Conservative Party were ousted at the May 1 election.

Straw said he hoped the judge could report by the end of the year. He told parliament that if any evidence had been overlooked during three previous inquiries he would take whatever action was necessary.
